documents.title: Maharashtra Shops and Establishments (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 2017
documents.ministry: Department of Labour, Government of Maharashtra
documents.description: Regulates terms of employment, working hours, overtime wages, leaves, and women employment conditions in all shops, offices, and commercial establishments throughout Maharashtra.

sections.title: Daily and weekly hours of work in shops and establishments
sections.originalText: (1) No adult worker shall be required or allowed to work in any establishment for more than nine hours in any day and forty-eight hours in any week: Provided that, the total number of hours of work including overtime shall not exceed ten and a half hours in any day and sixty hours in any week, subject to the conditions that the overtime hours shall not exceed one hundred and twenty-five hours in a period of three continuous months. (2) No worker shall be required to work continuously for more than five hours without an interval for rest of at least half an hour.
sections.simplifiedText: In Maharashtra, no shop, IT firm, or office employee can be compelled to work more than 9 hours in a single day or 48 hours in a week. Continuous work cannot exceed 5 hours without at least a 30-minute rest break. Maximum permissible overtime is 125 hours per quarter.

sections.title: Wages for overtime work
sections.originalText: Where a worker in any establishment is required to work beyond nine hours on any day or forty-eight hours in any week, he shall, in respect of such overtime work, be entitled to wages at the rate of twice his ordinary rate of wages. Explanation.—For the purposes of this section, "ordinary rate of wages" means the basic wages plus such allowances, including the cash equivalent of the advantage accruing through the concessional sale to workers of foodgrains and other articles, as the worker is for the time being entitled to, but does not include a bonus.
sections.simplifiedText: Any employee in Maharashtra working beyond 9 hours in a day or 48 hours in a week is legally entitled to overtime pay at double (2x) their ordinary wage rate (basic salary + allowances).

sections.title: Leave with wages and casual leaves
sections.originalText: (1) Every worker who has worked for not less than two hundred and forty days in an establishment during a calendar year shall be allowed in the subsequent calendar year, leave with wages at the rate of one day for every twenty days of work performed by him. (2) Every worker shall be entitled to eight days of casual leave with wages in every calendar year. (3) If a worker does not in any one calendar year take the whole of the leave allowed to him under sub-section (1), any leave not taken by him shall be added to the leave to be allowed to him in the succeeding calendar year: Provided that, the total number of days of leave that may be carried forward shall not exceed forty-five days.
sections.simplifiedText: Employees in Maharashtra are entitled to 1 earned paid leave for every 20 days worked (approx. 18-20 days/year) plus 8 mandatory casual leaves with full pay. Unused earned leaves can be accumulated and carried forward up to a maximum of 45 days.

sections.title: Prohibition of discrimination and protection of women workers
sections.originalText: (1) No woman worker shall be discriminated against in matters of recruitment, training, transfers or promotion or wages on ground of sex. (2) No woman worker shall be required or allowed to work in any establishment except between the hours of 7 a.m. and 9-30 p.m.: Provided that, the woman worker with her consent may be allowed to work during 9-30 p.m. and 7-00 a.m. in any establishment where the employer provides adequate shelter, rest rooms, safe transportation from the establishment to the doorstep of her residence, night creche and proper protection of their dignity, honour and safety, and protection from sexual harassment.
sections.simplifiedText: Women employees in Maharashtra cannot be paid less or discriminated against for promotions based on sex. Night shifts (between 9:30 PM and 7:00 AM) are strictly optional and require prior written consent, along with employer-provided doorstep pick-up/drop transportation, security, and ICC protection.

documents.title: Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999
documents.ministry: Department of Housing, Government of Maharashtra
documents.description: Unified tenancy and rent control law in Maharashtra governing fixation of standard rent, tenant eviction protection, and summary recovery of leave and license residential premises.

sections.title: Fixation of standard rent and permitted increases
sections.originalText: (1) Subject to the provisions of section 9, upon an application made to it for that purpose, or in any suit or proceedings, the court may fix the standard rent at such amount as, having regard to the provisions of this Act and the circumstances of the case, the court deems just. (2) It shall not be lawful for any landlord to claim or receive on account of the rent for any premises any increase above the standard rent, except where an increase is permitted by this Act.
sections.simplifiedText: A landlord in Maharashtra cannot arbitrarily hike rent beyond permitted statutory increases. Either tenant or landlord can approach the Small Causes Court (in Mumbai) or Civil Judge to determine and fix the legal standard rent.

sections.title: No ejectment ordinarily to be made if tenant pays or is ready and willing to pay standard rent
sections.originalText: (1) A landlord shall not be entitled to the recovery of possession of any premises so long as the tenant pays, or is ready and willing to pay, the amount of the standard rent and permitted increases, if any, and observes and performs the other conditions of the tenancy, in so far as they are consistent with the provisions of this Act. (2) No suit for recovery of possession shall be instituted by a landlord against a tenant on the ground of non-payment of the standard rent or permitted increases, until the expiration of ninety days next after notice in writing demanding the rent has been served upon the tenant.
sections.simplifiedText: Tenants in Maharashtra cannot be evicted as long as they are regularly paying the standard rent and abiding by tenancy terms. A landlord must serve a mandatory 90-day written demand notice before any eviction suit for non-payment can even be filed.

sections.title: Members of public or licensors entitled to recover possession of premises given on licence on expiry
sections.originalText: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, a licensee in possession or occupation of premises given to him on licence for residence shall deliver possession of such premises to the licensor on the expiry of the period of licence; and on the failure of the licensee to so deliver the possession of the licensed premises, a licensor shall be entitled to recover possession of such premises by making an application to the Competent Authority. (2) Any licensee who does not deliver possession of the premises to the licensor on expiry of the period of licence shall be liable to pay damages at double the rate of the licence fee or charge of the premises fixed under the agreement of licence.
sections.simplifiedText: For residential Leave and License agreements in Maharashtra, a licensee must vacate when the agreement expires. If they refuse to leave, the landlord can apply directly to the Competent Authority (Rent Authority) for summary eviction, and the overstaying licensee must pay double (2x) the monthly license fee as statutory penalty.

documents.title: Maharashtra State Legal Services Authority Rules, 1998
documents.description: Prescribes the income ceiling and eligibility conditions for free legal services, panel advocates, and legal advice through SLSAs and DLSAs in the State of Maharashtra.

sections.title: Income ceiling for entitlement to free legal services in Maharashtra
sections.originalText: A citizen whose annual income from all sources does not exceed Rs. 3,00,000 (Rupees Three Lakhs only) shall be entitled to free legal services under clause (h) of section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 in cases before the High Court of Bombay and all subordinate courts and tribunals in Maharashtra. Provided that this income limit shall not apply to women, children, members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, persons with disabilities, victims of human trafficking or disaster, and industrial workmen, who are entitled to free legal aid unconditionally.
sections.simplifiedText: In Maharashtra, any citizen earning less than ₹3,00,000 per year is entitled to completely free legal aid (free court advocate, filing costs, and paperwork) via the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA). Women, children, SC/ST citizens, disabled persons, and industrial workers get free legal aid regardless of their income.

documents.title: Delhi Shops and Establishments Act, 1954
documents.ministry: Labour Department, Government of NCT of Delhi
documents.description: Regulates conditions of work and employment in shops and commercial establishments in the National Capital Territory of Delhi, including wage payment timelines, work hours, and dismissal notice.

sections.title: Daily and weekly hours of work and rest intervals in Delhi
sections.originalText: (1) No adult employee shall be required or allowed to work in any establishment for more than nine hours in any day and forty-eight hours in any week. (2) The periods of work of adult employees in an establishment shall be so fixed that no period shall exceed five hours and that no employee shall work for more than five hours before he has had an interval for rest of at least half an hour.
sections.simplifiedText: In Delhi, shop and office employees cannot be made to work more than 9 hours a day or 48 hours a week. A mandatory rest interval of at least 30 minutes must be provided after every 5 continuous hours of work.

sections.title: Time and conditions of payment of wages in Delhi
sections.originalText: (1) Every employer shall fix periods in respect of which such wages shall be payable. (2) No wage-period shall exceed one month. (3) The wages of every person employed in any establishment shall be paid before the expiry of the seventh day after the last day of the wage-period in respect of which the wages are payable.
sections.simplifiedText: In Delhi, every employer must pay monthly salaries on or before the 7th day of the succeeding month. Withholding salary past the 7th is a statutory violation.

sections.title: Leave privileges: annual privilege leave, sickness, and casual leave
sections.originalText: (1) Every person employed in an establishment shall be entitled after twelve months continuous employment to privilege leave with full wages for a total period of not less than fifteen days. (2) Every person employed in an establishment shall also be entitled during every twelve months of continuous service to sickness leave on half wages for not less than twelve days and casual leave with full wages for not less than twelve days on medical certificate or urgent private affairs.
sections.simplifiedText: Delhi employees are entitled to at least 15 days of annual paid privilege leave, 12 days of casual leave with full pay, and 12 days of sick leave per year.

sections.title: Notice of dismissal and protection from arbitrary termination
sections.originalText: (1) No employer shall dispense with the services of an employee who has been in his continuous employment for not less than three months without giving such employee at least one month’s notice in writing or wages in lieu of such notice: Provided that such notice shall not be necessary where the services of such employee are dispensed with for misconduct. (2) No employee who has put in at least three months continuous service shall terminate his employment without giving his employer at least one month’s notice in writing.
sections.simplifiedText: An employer in Delhi cannot terminate an employee who has completed 3 months of service without providing at least 1 month of prior written notice or 1 month of salary in lieu of notice (unless terminated for proven gross misconduct after an inquiry).

documents.title: Delhi (Right of Citizen to Time Bound Delivery of Services) Act, 2011
documents.ministry: Administrative Reforms Department, Government of NCT of Delhi
documents.description: Guarantees the right of citizens in Delhi to time-bound delivery of government services, statutory grievance redressal, and compensatory penalties from defaulting officers.

sections.title: Right to time bound delivery of public services in Delhi
sections.originalText: Every citizen shall have the right to time bound delivery of notified citizen services by the competent government departments, municipal corporations, and autonomous bodies within the stipulated time limit specified in the schedule.
sections.simplifiedText: Citizens residing in Delhi have a legally enforceable right to obtain notified government documents (birth/caste/income certificates, driving licenses, ration cards, water/electricity connections) within fixed statutory days.

sections.title: Compensatory cost payable to citizen for delay in public services
sections.originalText: Where the competent authority fails to deliver the notified service within the stipulated time limit without reasonable justification, the citizen shall be entitled to compensatory cost at the rate of Rs. 10 to Rs. 200 per day of delay, subject to a maximum of Rs. 5,000, which shall be recovered directly from the salary of the defaulting government official.
sections.simplifiedText: If a Delhi government department delays your notified certificate or application past the deadline without valid cause, you are legally entitled to compensation of up to ₹200 per day of delay (max ₹5,000), deducted directly from the defaulting officer’s salary.

documents.title: Delhi State Legal Services Authority Regulations, 2018
documents.description: Establishes income eligibility guidelines, front office helpdesks, and legal aid clinics across all 11 Delhi district courts for free legal representation.

sections.title: Eligibility criteria and income threshold for free legal services in Delhi
sections.originalText: Under section 12(h) of the Act, a resident of Delhi whose annual income does not exceed Rs. 3,00,000 (Rupees Three Lakhs only) is entitled to free legal aid in all courts and tribunals across Delhi. Women, children, SC/ST citizens, transgender persons, senior citizens with limited means, and victims of crime are eligible without any income barrier upon submitting an application to DSLSA (dslsa.org or Helpline 1516).
sections.simplifiedText: Any Delhi resident earning less than ₹3,00,000/year qualifies for 100% free legal representation from DSLSA. Women, children, SC/ST, and transgender persons are eligible with zero income limits. Call Delhi Legal Aid Helpline 1516 or visit any district court front office.

documents.title: Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961
documents.ministry: Department of Labour, Government of Karnataka
documents.description: Governs working hours, rest intervals, weekly off, termination notice, and health safety conditions for commercial and IT establishments across Karnataka.

sections.title: Daily and weekly hours of work in Karnataka commercial establishments
sections.originalText: (1) No employee in any establishment shall be required or allowed to work for more than nine hours on any day and forty-eight hours in any week: Provided that the total number of hours of work including overtime shall not exceed ten hours in any day and fifty-four hours in any week. (2) No employee shall be required or allowed to work continuously for more than five hours unless he has had an interval for rest of at least one hour.
sections.simplifiedText: In Karnataka (including Bengaluru tech parks), no employee can be made to work more than 9 hours a day or 48 hours a week. A mandatory rest break of at least 1 hour is required after 5 continuous hours of work.

sections.title: Compulsory weekly holiday
sections.originalText: (1) Every establishment shall remain closed on one day of the week. The employer shall fix such day at the beginning of the year and notify it to the Inspector. (2) It shall not be lawful for an employer to call an employee at, or for an employee to go to, his establishment or any other place for any work in connection with the business on his weekly holiday.
sections.simplifiedText: Every establishment in Karnataka must provide at least one full day of weekly rest to every employee. Employers cannot compel employees to do any work on their designated weekly off.

sections.title: Notice of termination of employment in Karnataka
sections.originalText: (1) No employer shall remove or dismiss an employee who has been in his continuous employment for not less than six months without reasonable cause and without giving such employee at least one month’s notice in writing or wages in lieu thereof: Provided that such notice shall not be necessary where the services of such employee are dispensed with on a charge of misconduct supported by satisfactory evidence recorded at an inquiry held for the purpose.
sections.simplifiedText: In Karnataka, an employer cannot dismiss an employee with over 6 months of service without reasonable cause and at least 1 month prior written notice or 1 month salary in lieu of notice.

documents.title: Karnataka Guarantee of Services to Citizens Act (Sakala), 2011
documents.ministry: Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms, Government of Karnataka
documents.description: Sakala mission providing statutory guarantee of time-bound delivery of over 1,000 public citizen services in Karnataka with automated compensatory delay penalties.

sections.title: Citizen right to receive public services within stipulated time (Sakala)
sections.originalText: Every eligible citizen shall have the right to obtain the citizen-related service from the designated public servant within the stipulated time limit specified under the Sakala mission for the respective department.
sections.simplifiedText: Under Karnataka’s Sakala Act, citizens have a legal right to receive caste certificates, khata extracts, building permits, and driving licenses within statutory deadlines tracked via a unique 15-digit GSC number.

sections.title: Compensatory cost payable to citizen on default under Sakala
sections.originalText: If the designated public servant fails to provide the citizen-related service within the stipulated time limit or rejects the application without valid grounds, the citizen shall be entitled to compensatory cost at the rate of Rs. 20 per day of default, subject to a maximum of Rs. 500, to be paid to the applicant.
sections.simplifiedText: Under Sakala in Karnataka, if your application is delayed without lawful justification, the government must pay you compensatory costs (₹20/day) recovered from the defaulting officer’s pay.

documents.title: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Rules, 1996
documents.description: Prescribes the income ceiling and eligibility parameters for free legal assistance across all district and taluka courts in Karnataka.

sections.title: Income limit for free legal aid in Karnataka
sections.originalText: Under section 12(h) of the Act, a person whose annual income from all sources does not exceed Rs. 3,00,000 (Rupees Three Lakhs only) is entitled to free legal aid in cases before the High Court of Karnataka and all subordinate civil and criminal courts in Karnataka. Women, children, SC/ST, and disabled persons are entitled unconditionally.
sections.simplifiedText: In Karnataka, any resident with an annual family income of up to ₹3,00,000 is eligible for completely free legal services through KSLSA and DLSAs. Women, children, and SC/ST citizens qualify automatically without any income restriction.
